root_cause.text: In the `usb_keene_probe()` function, the v4l2 control handler is initialized and controls are added, but the error paths after `v4l2_device_register()` or `video_register_device()` fail did not call `v4l2_ctrl_handler_free()`, causing a memory leak of the control handler.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that if `v4l2_device_register()` or `video_register_device()` fails afterward, the handler was never freed. The patch diff moves the `v4l2_ctrl_handler_free()` call to the `err_v4l2` label to cover all error paths after initialization.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove redundant v4l2_ctrl_handler_free in error path of usb_keene_probe to avoid double-free since the handler is freed in the common cleanup label.
intent_record.what: Removed the call to v4l2_ctrl_handler_free(hdl) from the error handling path in usb_keene_probe when hdl->error is set.
intent_record.how: Previously, when hdl->error was non-zero, the handler was freed before jumping to the err_v4l2 label, which may have caused a double-free if err_v4l2 also frees the handler or other resources. Now the handler is not freed at that point, likely relying on the cleanup at err_v4l2 to handle it appropriately.

intent_record.what: Added a call to v4l2_ctrl_handler_free(&radio->hdl) in the error handling path of usb_keene_probe after the err_v4l2 label, before kfree(radio->buffer).
intent_record.how: This ensures that the V4L2 control handler is properly freed when a probe error occurs after its initialization, preventing a memory leak.
